bluf: Digital Remedy is a US performance media specialist selling Performance TV across CTV, OTT, linear, audio and DOOH to mid market brands, with outcome measurement and an in house AI assistant, RemyAI. The Horus read puts it in the Tailwind band at the 95th percentile, while the Monsoon read puts it in the Doldrums: little of what it sells moves offshore. The one thing a rival should know: the public book is one named client, Machete, with no described work, and the headline is a single 1,738% ROAS claim. It is likely selling on measurement, not on a client list.
doing:
The positioning line, in the record's words, is a performance media company reimagining performance marketing via Performance TV, Action and Brand solutions spanning CTV, OTT, linear, audio and DOOH, with outcome measurement. In plain words: a television and streaming buyer that sells the buy as a performance channel and the measurement of it as the product. The headline claim showcases a fast casual brand earning 1,738% ROAS from Performance CTV; the record holds no named client behind the figure.

The sold mix is narrow (breadth 3). Programmatic & CTV leads at score 3: the meta leads with OTT, CTV and performance TV, 50+ premium OTT publishers, and linear, YouTube TV, audio and DOOH buying. Two core lines sit at score 2: AI Automation / Agents, on the homepage section promoting RemyAI, and Data & Measurement, on a suite of TV attribution, brand lift, incrementality and halo effect with incremental sales lift case studies. Proprietary products on record: RemyAI, the Digital Remedy Creative Suite and VoterReach, district level political media reporting. The record lists no partners. Every other capability scores 0.

The AI posture is RemyAI, an in house assistant that answers questions on campaign data with instant reports, visualisations and optimisation recommendations; the Horus read scores that as partial on P6 and absent on P1, P2 and P7. The pricing signal is specific: it pitches linear TV buying with lower minimum spend requirements than usual national and local buys, yet no public pricing model shows (P5 unknown).

The record lists no moves, news, deepened case studies or jobs, so there is no dated trail. Conspicuously absent for a paid media specialist: no paid search or paid social line at all, no first party data or CRM line and no partners, which leaves the measurement suite and the assistant as the only things a buyer can hold it to.
clients:
The client type is mid market; the record lists verticals of QSR and restaurants, CPG and pet food, fintech, B2B technology and SaaS, travel and airlines, legal, fashion, real estate, automotive accessories, auto insurance and political campaigns, with VoterReach and its LinkedIn ads aimed at the last of these. The home market is the US; no office is listed.

The book on record is one name: Machete, from a case study whose URL slug reads advanced feature creatives, with no described work, so the record reads it as named only (1 of 1, observed 0). With no signal, the need is inferred from what Digital Remedy leads with: paid performance on CTV and OTT with data and measurement behind it; the slug points at creative work through its Creative Suite, an inference. No shared clients appear on other tracked agencies' books (shared 0). The fast casual brand behind the 1,738% ROAS headline is unnamed in the record.

The rest of who it serves must be read from the verticals and the ads: the LinkedIn samples sell VoterReach reporting that maps media investment to congressional and state legislative districts, and a Measurement Blueprint with a maturity matrix, which points at political buyers and measurement led marketers rather than any named account.

What the base needs next, tied to the edition: with KJ4 (The platforms are absorbing the execution layer) and KJ6 (The agency middle is being hollowed out) both tailwinds for it, it is likely, with low confidence given one named client, that its buyers ask for incrementality proof rather than more buying hours, and a roughly even chance that KJ5 (The price of attention splits in two) reprices the CTV inventory it leads with, its one headwind.

market:
The Horus read: tailwind index 36.9, band Tailwind, 95th percentile, integrity unscored. Best placed for KJ4 (The platforms are absorbing the execution layer, net 0.75), driven by Data & Measurement at +2 and AI Automation / Agents at +1, and for KJ6 (The agency middle is being hollowed out, net 0.579), on the same two lines. Most exposed to KJ5 (The price of attention splits in two, net -0.289) through Programmatic & CTV. Best fit: The Bazaar of Agents at 43/100. P moves: partial on P6; absent on P1, P2 and P7; unknown on P5; P3, P4 and P8 not applicable.

The Monsoon read: index 32.3, band Doldrums, 5th percentile, migration 29.8 against displacement 34.8. The verdict puts 30 of the index on the sold mix, Data & Measurement (13) and AI Automation / Agents (11) carrying the most movable hours, and sends 65% of the work to South and Southeast Asia and 25% to Latin America; the class is inferred, no hub office is listed, and the read counts the in house RemyAI description as an onshore claim.
openings:
The strongest opening is the empty book. One named client, Machete, with no described work, against an unnamed 1,738% ROAS headline: it is likely, with moderate confidence, that a rival with named CTV case studies wins a measurement led pitch against it. The falsifier: the next compile finding named case studies with described work behind the ROAS figure.

Price is second. It pitches lower minimum spend for linear TV yet publishes no pricing model (P5 unknown): a transparent, outcome priced CTV offer is a conversation it cannot have in public, a roughly even chance of forcing it there. On the Monsoon Doldrums read (32.3) an offshore delivered rival gains little: the offer that undercuts it is proof, not cheaper hours.

Third, the headwind. Its lead line, Programmatic & CTV, is the only driver of its KJ5 exposure (net -0.289): the premium OTT inventory it leads with (50+ publishers) is the contestable end. The political vertical, sold through VoterReach, is the one it defends with a product; the other verticals it lists are contestable by any measurement first buyer, and it is very unlikely, with high confidence, to contest search, social or creator work, where it scores 0.
